title: Staleness reconciliation proto - personal notebook
content:
Quick personal notes for a proto design around reconciling stale/pending client-side + runtime KV cache shards. Goal: reduce visible regressions for long-lived sessions where partial context updates arrive out of order, or where offline client merges have conflicting patches. This is a trimmed sketch — rough ideas, heuristics, and a tiny API shape.

Background / problem statement:
- We shard conversational context into compact KV segments (anchors, slots, short embeddings). Clients can prefetch, update, and evict segments; runtime maintains a server-side KV cache for fast reuse.
- Multiple sources of truth: client-local edits (optimistic), server-rollups (from other clients or background sync), and on-the-wire partial reconstructions. Race conditions cause: visible staleness (client shows old facts), duplication, and hallucination when model relies on stale anchors.
- Need a reconciliation protocol that: (a) is low-latency for reads, (b) is robust to partial apply failures, (c) gives a score/trace for staleness so downstream ranking/fallbacks can use it.

Design goals (prioritized):
1) Signal staleness with bounded overhead (small per-kv metadata).
2) Support cheap on-read merge attempts when client provides lightweight hints.
3) Allow async server-side reconciliation without blocking main inference path.
4) Provide deterministic tie-breaks for conflict resolution (owner, lamport-ish counter, epoch).

Core concepts / primitives:
- kv-segment: an immutable delta bundle for a logical context slice. id = sha256(namespace || sequence || owner).
- attribs: metadata (owner_id, epoch, sequence, tombstone, last-sync-ts, staleness-weight). Small vector of strings/ints.
- staleness-score: float 0..1 (0 fresh, 1 maximally stale). Computed from epoch distance, sequence gaps, last-sync age, and probabilistic freshness model.
- reconciliation-hint: optional blob client can send with requests: {known_epochs: [id:epoch], preferred_owner: id, apply_policy: fast|safe|predictive}.

Runtime behaviour sketches:
- read path (fast): attempt local cache hit, attach staleness-score per segment. If score > threshold (0.4) and request latency budget allows, enqueue background fetch+merge. Return base result + staleness annotations.
- read path (safe): if apply_policy==safe then block read until server-side merge completes or small timeout (50-100ms).
- write path: client sends delta bundle with attribs. Runtime attempts atomic apply to local shard index; returns resolved id and new epoch. If conflict detected (incoming epoch <= local epoch), runtime replies with conflict metadata (local_epoch, remote_epoch, resolution_hint).

Lightweight API shapes (proto-ish examples)
- POST /kv/delta/apply
  body: { "owner": "user_123", "deltas": [{"slot":"anchor-3","blob": "base64...","seq": 44, "epoch": 2025}], "client_hint": {"last_known_epochs": [{"slot":"anchor-3","epoch":200}] } }
  response: { "applied": [{"slot":"anchor-3","id":"sha256...","epoch":2025}], "conflicts": [{"slot":"anchor-7","local_epoch":210,"incoming_epoch":208,"resolution":"noop"}], "latency_ms": 12 }

- GET /kv/context?session=abc&slots=anchor-3,slot-1
  headers: X-Recon-Hint: {"apply_policy":"fast","preferred_owner":"user_123"} (encoded)
  response: { "context": [{"slot":"anchor-3","id":"sha256..","epoch":2025,"staleness":0.12,"resolution_hint":null}], "meta": {"fetch_async": true} }

Reconciliation procedure (async worker):
1) gather candidates: local shard + remote rollup + recent client deltas (within last N seconds).
2) build candidate timeline sorted by epoch, then seq, then owner-priority (owner_last_write wins).
3) merge algorithm: for simple key/value or slot replace, pick latest non-tombstone. For structured anchors (lists, summaries) run a small merge function (3-way diff heuristic) and emit a reconciliation-delta with provenance.
4) commit reconciliation delta as new kv-segment (new epoch++) and publish a minimal watch-signal to sessions that subscribe.

Staleness scoring ideas (hybrid):
- base = clamp( (now - last_sync) / ttl , 0, 1 )
- epoch_gap = sigmoid( (current_epoch - local_epoch) / gap_scale )
- op_confidence = 1 - (num_conflicting_writes / (1 + num_writes))
- staleness = weighted_sum([base, epoch_gap, 1-op_confidence])
Note: keep weights configurable per-tenant.

Instrumentation / observability:
- expose per-request staleness histogram and correlation with downstream quality metrics (edit loss, user-rollback rate).
- trace id should include per-slot staleness to visualize which anchors cause regressions.

Fallback policies (examples):
- if staleness > 0.7 and model indicates high-likelihood factual query, route to conservative-mode model or ask clarifying question.
- if staleness in [0.4, 0.7], return result with a soft disclaimer + surfaced provenance.
- allow client-side override: client signals to ignore staleness if UX requires speed.

Edge cases & open questions (TODOs):
- partial apply failures when reconciliation worker cannot build deterministic merge (e.g., semantic conflicts). How to present to user? (options: create fork, mark stale, prompt human).
- eviction interplay: when runtime evicts a segment, clients may still reference older ids. Need TTL+ghost tombstone pattern to let late reconciles succeed.
- cross-device causal ordering: do we provide a causality token per-session? Lamport counters are simple but may not reflect real causality across offline edits.
- cost model: background reconciliation increases IOPS — need heuristics to avoid hot churn on active sessions. LRU + hot-lease concept?

Prototype checklist (next steps):
- [ ] implement tiny staleness scorer lib (js + go) and run synthetic sim against recorded session traces.
- [ ] add per-slot staleness header to runtime read path (non-blocking) and collect histograms.
- [ ] sketch reconciliation worker WIP in runtime repo (link above).
- [ ] UX experiment: small A/B on safe vs fast apply policy for 2 product flows (compose vs search).

Simple ASCII diagram (read + async recon flow):

Client                 Runtime               Reconciler Worker    Storage/Remote rollup
  |---GET context----->| cache hit? (annotate) |                    |
  |<--context + staleness-| (if high score) enqueue fetch ->|                 |
  |                       |----------------------->fetch other shards-->|
  |                       |<-------publish recon-delta--------|                 |
  |<-(optional watch)----| notify client of new epoch/id     |                 |

Notes to self: keep the client hint payload tiny (max 2–3 slot entries for typical interactive call). Consider moving heavy merge to an offline batch job that runs at low priority.

Open items to discuss with Priya/Ethan in sync:
- ordering semantics we commit to (strong session order vs eventual per-slot)
- cheap watch primitives — use SSE or ephemeral websocket share?
- how to present reconciliation provenance in RLHF/eval logs (so we can detect model regressions caused by stale shards)

End — will refine into a short PRD once sim results show the staleness score correlates with user-visible errors.
